title: The Hidden Danger of Back-Graded Waste Pipes
description: One of the most frequent errors in drainage installation is failing to maintain a proper downward slope on horizontal waste pipes, a mistake known as back-grading or reverse slope. When a waste pipe slopes upward or sits completely flat away from the fixture, wastewater loses its momentum. Solid waste settles at the low points instead of carrying through to the main sewer line, leading to persistent, recurring clogs. Professional drainage installation relies on gravity and consistent fall to clear waste effectively. Always verify your pipe alignment with a spirit level before securing hangers and finalizing connections to prevent costly callbacks.
